hook: The Corona Heights site the city dedicated to Josephine Randall in 1951 as its junior museum.

parcel.note: The assessor's roll files this parcel as public open space at 122 States Street; its 721,266 sq ft lot area and $0 assessed value are for the whole of Corona Heights Park, not the museum building alone, and the 1,338 sq ft building area and other structural figures are minimal for a museum whose 2014–2018 permits describe a full interior renovation. EAS separately carries 199 Museum Way as this parcel's address, which is the museum's own; several of its own building permits name it the Randall Museum.

assessment.note: Publicly owned parkland carries no assessed value on the roll; no land/improvement split is charted.

present_use.name: Randall Museum
present_use.note: DBI's own permit descriptions name the building "the Randall Museum," e.g. permit 201512185449.

historic_status.ceqa_status_label: Historical resource; eligible California Register historic district

permits.description: A new cafe and prep kitchen built as a tenant improvement.
New electrical service installed, amending the scope of an earlier renovation permit.
Countertops and sinks replaced, and electrical outlets in the counter areas replaced; layouts unchanged.
Evacuation maps posted for the basement, first and mezzanine floors.
A new addressable fire alarm system installed, with sprinkler monitoring, elevator recall, fire door release and full building coverage.
117 new sprinklers installed for the lower-level renovation, with a new fire service line off Roosevelt Way.
Partial demolition of walls and interior renovation of the STEM lab and toddler room at the Randall Museum, including electrical, lighting and finishes.

A primarily interior renovation: new geology and zoology exhibits, a renovated live-animal exhibit, science lab, multipurpose room, three bathrooms, lobby and concession and office areas, plus a new elevator and accessibility upgrades.
A concrete patio and accessible ramp added, a storage area and entrance gate added, and the garage repaired.

permit_summary.note: Four filings on this parcel are omitted: two nominal-cost inspection renewals and a final-inspection permit that only reference the substantive permits shown, and a $1 permit for the underground portion of the 2016 sprinkler work.

historical_record.summary: Junior museum opens at Corona Heights
historical_record.description: The Josephine D. Randall Junior Museum opened at Corona Heights, dedicated in honor of Josephine Randall, the city's superintendent of recreation for twenty-five years; the Recreation and Park Commission suspended its rule against naming buildings for living people to do so.
The $12 million bond measure's funds were finally appropriated, and construction of the new museum building began.
San Francisco voters passed a $12 million bond measure to fund a new Junior Museum building.
The Recreation Commission set aside the Corona Heights site for the museum.

historical_record.summary: City purchases the Corona Heights lot
historical_record.description: The San Francisco Board of Supervisors purchased the Corona Heights lot for $27,333.
